findings.title: The raw ES `_id` is used as the saved object id, so the AAD never matches and decryption always fails.
findings.body: The `_id` metadata column holds the raw document id that the serializer builds, `[namespace:]type:id` (for example `index-pattern:abc` or `space1:connector:abc`). It does not hold the saved object id. Passing it as `id` to `decryptOrStripResponseAttributes` builds the wrong AAD, so every encrypted attribute in `_source` fails to decrypt and is stripped. The documented "decrypted in `_source`" path never works. The descriptor is also built only from `source.namespaces`. Single-namespace types store their space in `source.namespace`, so the AAD namespace is wrong for them as well. Fix: parse the raw id the way the serializer does (`serializer.rawToSavedObject`, or strip the `namespace:type:` prefix) and pass the real namespace for single-namespace types.

findings.title: Encrypted ciphertext in `_source` is returned untouched when `_id` is missing or a column is renamed.
findings.body: `decryptSourceColumn` skips all processing unless there is a column named exactly `_source` and one named exactly `_id`. `stripEncryptedColumns` never touches `_source`. So `metadata: ['_source']` without `_id`, or a pipeline such as `| RENAME _source AS src`, sends encrypted attribute values to the caller as-is. That contradicts the tutorial's promise that they are decrypted or stripped. The unit test at esql.test.ts:410 locks in this leak. Fix: when `_source` is present but cannot be decrypted, strip encrypted attributes from it (using `getEncryptedAttributes`) instead of returning it unchanged. Also consider rejecting renames of `_source`.

findings.title: Leftover agent task files are committed to the repository.
findings.body: `tasks/prd.json` and `tasks/progress.txt` are working notes from the agent loop (branch name, user-story progress, learnings). They are not part of the feature, add top-level files to Kibana, and the request does not cover them. Remove them from the PR.

findings.title: Agent progress log is committed to the repository.
findings.body: This is a scratch log from the agent run. The request does not need it, so it should not be merged. Remove the file.

findings.title: Encrypted columns are found only by exact name, so renaming or deriving a column bypasses stripping.
findings.body: Columns are nulled only when their name is exactly `${type}.${attr}`. A pipeline such as `| EVAL s = connector.secrets` or `| RENAME connector.secrets AS s` (or `CONCAT`, `STATS VALUES(...)`) returns the encrypted value under another name, untouched. This applies whenever the encrypted attribute is mapped and readable by ES|QL; I could not check the mappings of every encrypted type. Fix: inspect the pipeline for references to encrypted fields, or exclude them with a `DROP`/filter before the user pipeline runs, so the check does not depend on the output column names.

held.title: The composer is imported from `@elastic/esql`, not the `@kbn/esql-language` package the PR describes.
held.body: The PR description and the PRD say the `esql` composer comes from `@kbn/esql-language`. This file imports `esql` from `@elastic/esql` and relies on `esql.from(indices, metadata).print()`. If that package is not a declared dependency of this core package, or its `from` API differs, building the FROM clause fails at build or run time. I could not verify the package or its API from here. Fix: import from the intended package and declare it in the package's dependencies.
